transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Qorex Head of AI), Lena Ortiz (Product Lead), Michael Zhou (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough): Discussed POC success criteria for quality eval, agreement on golden prompts set size, regression test cadence, hallucination and format checks, scoring approach (pass/fail thresholds + weighted metrics), workload sizing for benchmarks, and initial timeline for a 4-week POC pilot. Action items and next steps agreed.

Topics: success criteria; golden prompts; regression tests; hallucination checks; format validation; scoring rubric; sample size and bench sizing; timeline and security checklist.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro, I'm Alex, AE on this account, and Priya is going to run the tech part.
[00:08] Priya Rao: hi all, Priya here. we'll try to keep this practical, focus on what you need to prove in the pilot to make a decision.
[00:14] Samir Patel: hi, thanks. quick context: Qorex is building a conversational assistant for compliance ops. our main worries are hallucinations and strict formatting for regulatory reports. we want to see measurable improvement over our current in-house LLM pipeline.
[00:29] Lena Ortiz: and from product, timeline is tight—stakeholders want an exec review in early August so we need a POC that shows clear pass/fail metrics.
[00:39] Michael Zhou: SRE side: we need latency and throughput numbers, VPC details, and how keys are handled. encryption at rest is a must.

[00:48] Priya Rao: ok great — our recommended scope for the quality eval is three pillars: 1) Golden prompt set and acceptance criteria, 2) Automated regression tests (hallucination + format checks), and 3) Benchmarks (latency, p50/p95, and cost-per-1k tokens).
[01:05] Alex Chen: to add, we usually recommend at least 1k to 5k representative prompts for the pilot depending on diversity; for golden set specifically we suggest a compact golden set of ~200 cases that cover critical edge cases.
[01:18] Samir Patel: 200 golden cases sounds right. we have a lot of corner-case regulatory templates—should those be in the golden set or in the larger sample?
[01:27] Priya Rao: put your most critical templates in the golden set — anything that would cause legal or compliance failure if misformatted. the larger 1k sample is for statistical checks and regression sensitivity.
[01:39] Lena Ortiz: how do you define "pass" for a golden case? is it exact match, fuzzy, or a combination?
[01:45] Priya Rao: good question. we propose a tiered scoring: exact-match for fixed-format fields (dates, identifiers), fuzzy semantic score for free text with a threshold (e.g., >= 0.8 embedding similarity or >80% on token-level match depending), plus a hallucination penalty when model invents unsupported facts. final pass when weighted score >= required threshold (we typically start with 0.85 overall).
[02:10] Samir Patel: embedding similarity feels a bit soft for compliance—can we do strict rules for the structured parts and semantic for narrative sections?
[02:18] Priya Rao: yes that's exactly the hybrid we recommend. structured validators for format + regex + checksum where applicable, and semantic similarity for narrative. hallucination detection runs as a separate check where we flag claims that don't appear in the source doc set.
[02:31] Alex Chen: we should capture concrete success criteria now: 1) Golden set pass rate >= 90% (weighted), 2) No high-severity hallucination in golden set, 3) p95 latency under 800ms in hosted mode or under your target in Dedicated, 4) Throughput target of X qps—Samir, what do you need?
[02:49] Samir Patel: for our peak we expect about 12 qps, average 3 qps. concurrency spikes to 40 for batch validation jobs. clearly stateable.
[02:57] Priya Rao: noted — we'll size the bench to 15 qps sustained and a burst test to 50 concurrent.
[03:04] Michael Zhou: for SRE, can you run a benchmark inside our VPC? we prefer private deployment for PII datasets.
[03:11] Priya Rao: yes we can run inside your VPC or run a dedicated runner that connects via peered network. we'll need firewall rules and a test NAT/IP; Michael you'll share details.
[03:20] Lena Ortiz: what's the scoring rubric look like — are there sub-metrics we track?
[03:24] Priya Rao: we'll provide a spreadsheet with columns: case_id, intent, expected_output, structural_score (0-1), semantic_score (0-1), hallucination_flag (0/1), final_weighted_score, comments. Weighting defaults: structured 0.5, semantic 0.4, hallucination penalty 0.1 (but can be tuned).
[03:43] Alex Chen: also cost metrics: cost per 10k tokens for the candidate model, and fallback model costs if we use multi-tier routing. we'll include that in the benchmark.
[03:52] Samir Patel: competitors question — we piloted with OpenAI and Cohere last quarter. can Redwood show where it improves on hallucination and cost?
[03:59] Priya Rao: yes we'll include side-by-side baseline runs using your supplied prompts against the models you used. small caveat: exact tokenization differences can shift numbers but relative hallucination rate and pass/fail on golden set are comparable.
[04:16] Alex Chen: timeline proposal: week 0 (this week) repository transfer + golden prompt draft, week 1-2 run bench and initial regression, week 3 refine prompts and run second pass, week 4 finalize report and exec summary. that gets you results by mid-July which fits your August review buffer.
[04:32] Lena Ortiz: mid-July is perfect. for reporting, we need an executive one-pager showing pass/fail and a technical appendix with sample failures.
[04:40] Priya Rao: we do both. the technical appendix will include failed cases with diffs and suggested prompt adjustments.
[04:45] Samir Patel: what about continuous regression after the pilot? we want weekly regressions against the golden set if we move to Dedicated.
[04:52] Priya Rao: we support automated weekly regression runs as part of Redwood Optimize; for Dedicated we can set retention and schedule.
[04:59] Michael Zhou: security — SOC2, KMS integration? and will logs include PII? we need redaction possibilities.
[05:07] Alex Chen: we'll send the security pack (SOC2 report, KMS options, VPC/on-prem notes). logs are configurable; we can redact or encrypt sensitive fields and provide audit logs.
[05:18] Samir Patel: is there an option to run the eval entirely offline/on-prem for the golden set?
[05:23] Priya Rao: yes, Private deployment is possible, though setup takes longer. for the pilot we recommend hosted inside a peered VPC runner to save time unless you insist on air-gapped.
[05:33] Alex Chen: ok to recap — agreed items: golden set size 200, larger sample 1k for stats, scoring rubric as hybrid structured+semantic with weights, hallucination detection flows, bench sizing 15 qps + 50 burst, latency p95 under 800ms target, timeline 4 weeks to deliver pilot results, security docs to be shared.
[05:51] Lena Ortiz: recap sounds good. any immediate blockers?
[05:55] Michael Zhou: i'll need to coordinate firewall and provide the test subnet by Tuesday.
[05:59] Samir Patel: we'll start extracting our templates and send Samir's team will send 200 golden cases and 1k sample prompts by Friday.
[06:07] Priya Rao: we'll draft the scoring spreadsheet and the hallucination/format validators and share by Thursday.
[06:12] Alex Chen: great — we'll follow up with the shared drive links and the benchmark schedule. thanks everyone.
[06:18] (meeting ends)
